items.title: Ahead of their time: Restricted to pre-2018 research, AI flags hydrogen catalyst reported in later experiments
items.excerpt: A large language model limited to pre-2018 literature flagged a Cr-Co-Fe-Mn-Ni alloy later reported as a hydrogen evolution electrocatalyst, and proposed new untested candidates (ACS Catalysis, DOI 10.1021/acscatal.6c00635).
items.rationale: Freshest item in the pool, with a clean test: an LLM limited to pre-2018 papers 'predicts' a catalyst found later, then proposes new untested ones.

items.title: AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants
items.excerpt: An AI 'virtual author' can help scientists apply a paper's methods to new data, though it does not match a human author's expertise.
items.rationale: A new way for researchers to use papers: a 'virtual author' agent re-applies a paper's methods to new data. The article also says plainly where it falls short.

items.title: Brain-inspired randomness makes artificial vision more reliable
items.excerpt: Hertie Institute researchers found that combining top-down feedback with simulated neural variability during training made recurrent vision networks markedly more robust to noise, attacks and distribution shift (Patterns, DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2026.101693).
items.rationale: A neuroscience-to-AI result: adding neural noise plus top-down feedback during training makes vision networks more robust (Patterns paper).

items.title: A crop-mapping benchmark for the tropics (PLANTEUR)
items.excerpt: PLANTEUR extends the PASTIS crop-mapping benchmark to six tropical regions to evaluate geospatial AI models across more diverse agricultural systems.
items.rationale: A primary-source benchmark release from Ai2 that fills the tropical gap in geospatial-AI crop-mapping evaluation, and adds an outlet the rest of the picks lack.

items.title: AI-powered robotic laboratory paves the way for discovering next-generation heat-resistant coatings
items.excerpt: University of Nottingham built a self-driving lab where robotic arms dispense, fire and retrieve samples while an active-learning AI picks which pyrochlore compositions to test as thermal barrier coatings (Eng. Appl. of AI, DOI 10.1016/j.engappai.2026.114993).
items.rationale: A new Nottingham self-driving lab: active learning picks which pyrochlore thermal-barrier coatings to test. Different institution, material and paper from the 10-18 bulk-metal testing story.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: (1) Phys.org 'Forecasting tipping points with AI climate simulation' is the same PNAS neural-operator study as EurekAlert 1147991 (science, 10-16). (2) Live Science '10 minutes of AI erodes motivation' is the same study as EurekAlert 1147258 (science, 10-10). (3) Physics World optical deepfake detection (97.8%) is the same work as ScienceDaily 260929053534 (science, 10-02). (4) Tech Xplore 'AI slays the dragon' Gemini agents in Minecraft is a cross-section dup of IGN google-ai-agents-killed-ender-dragon-minecraft (games, 10-21). (5) Microsoft Research KLS conjecture is held back as a probable repeat of SciAm 'AI solves a holy grail problem from probability theory' (science, 10-01). KLS is a probability and convex-geometry conjecture, and I could not verify the content without fetch tools. (6) Quanta 'AI proved the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. What happens now?' is analysis and reaction to an already-reported proof, near the 10-02 Riemann and 10-23 SciAm OpenAI-proof coverage, with no new event. Skipped on merit: Google Research Earth AI agents (the 10-07 Earth AI post is from the same product family, and this item is older), DeepMind antimicrobial discovery (10-15, staler; no published duplicate found), Science News 'AI can give you your voice back' (patient-facing feature that fits medicine better), and the MIT Q&A history interview (evergreen). Pre-filter story_dedup also dropped the desert-island Claude story and the MIT S2S weather story. Outlets: Phys.org x2, Science News, Tech Xplore, Ai2.
